([[2010–11 Israeli Basketball Super League|2011]], [[2015–16 Israeli Basketball Super League|2016]]) }} '''Gal Mekel''' ({{langx|he|גל מקל}}, pronounced {{IPA|he|ˈɡal ˈmekel|}}; born March 4, 1988){{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mekelga01.html|title=Gal Mekel Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com}} is an Israeli former professional [[basketball]] player. He played for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and spent time in Europe and Israel. He played [[college basketball]] for two years at [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State University]]. He then played in the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Super League]] for [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]], and [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]], and in the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A League]] for [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]]. He was a two-time [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP|Israeli Super League MVP]], in 2011 and 2013. He was the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Statistical Leaders#Assists leaders|Israeli Premier League Assists Leader]] in 2011 and 2016. In 2013, he signed a three-year minimum fully guaranteed contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], becoming the second Israeli to join the [[NBA]]; he also holds a [[Polish passport]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.shamsports.com/2013/07/mavericks-to-sign-gal-mekel-to-three.html|title=ShamSports {{!}} Mavericks to sign Gal Mekel to three year guaranteed deal|website=www.shamsports.com|date=July 2013|access-date=2020-10-28}}{{Dead link|date=May 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==Early and personal life== Mekel is [[Jewish]], and was born in [[Ramat HaSharon]], [[Israel]], to Alon and Ariela Mekel.{{cite journal|last=Ramati|first=Stan|title=Israeli Sports|journal=Jewish Sports Review|date=September–October 2013|volume=9|issue=99|page=9}}{{cite web|url=https://goshockers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/gal-mekel/2262 |title=#1 Gal Mekel |work=GoShockers.com |access-date=October 28, 2020}} He has four brothers and two sisters. He attended [[Alliance Israélite Universelle|Alliance High School]] in [[Tel Aviv]].{{cite web|last=Oliver |first=Ron |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Gal-Mekel/Events/7577 |title=Gal Mekel National and High School Stats, Dallas Mavericks |publisher=Basketball.realgm.com |access-date=November 9, 2013}} He started his way in the [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] youth team. Shortly after, he moved to the [[A.S. Ramat HaSharon]] youth team where he demonstrated a good playmaking ability. His ability caught the eyes of basketball giant [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], where he moved at the age of 17, and subsequently won the 2005–06 Israeli Youth League. His father-in-law was American-Israeli former basketball player [[Willie Sims (basketball)|Willie Sims]], after marrying daughter Danyella. ==College career== Mekel played [[college basketball]] for two years at [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]]. In his rookie season ([[2006–07 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2006–07]]), by mid-season he was promoted to starter. He finished his first season with averages of 13 minutes and four [[points per game]]. In the [[2007–08 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2007–08 season]], Mekel improved his stats to 9.3 ppg and 3.7 [[Assists per game|apg]] while playing more than 30 minutes per game. Despite his improvement he decided to leave the team after that season. ==Professional career== ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2008)=== On March 28, 2008, Mekel signed his first professional contract with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], for the remainder of the 2007–08 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/28382/180/maccabi-inks-guard-prospect-mekel |title=Maccabi inks guard prospect Mekel |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=March 28, 2008 |access-date=September 14, 2013}} ===Hapoel Gilboa Galil (2008–2009)=== For the [[2008–09 Israeli Basketball Super League|2008–09 season]], [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] [[loan (sports)|loaned]] Mekel to [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]], an Israeli club that is known for promoting young talents, in order to receive some playing experience, and return better the next year. In Galil, he averaged 6.9 points and 2.7 assists per game. He excelled in the league's playoff quarter-finals against [[Hapoel Holon]], helping his team reach the [[2008–2009 Israeli Final Four|Israeli Super League Final Four]], where they lost to Maccabi Tel Aviv. Mekel ended up winning the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Discovery of the Year|Israeli Super League Rising Star]] award.{{cite web|url=http://www.basket.co.il/News.asp?id=1469&lang=en |title=The 2008/09 BSL Season Awards |publisher=Basket.co.il |date=May 16, 2009 |access-date=September 14, 2013}} ===Return to Maccabi (2009)=== After a good season with Galil, Mekel returned to Maccabi Tel Aviv. They designated him at the [[point guard]] substitute spot, behind the team's newcomer [[Doron Perkins]], who had won the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Super League MVP]] award in the previous season.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/57942/180/maccabi-puts-perkins-mekel-at-point |title=Maccabi puts Perkins, Mekel at point |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=August 30, 2009 |access-date=September 14, 2013}} Mekel recorded 13 points and 5 assists in his debut game with Maccabi Tel Aviv, against [[Ironi Nahariya]], in the second round of the [[2009–10 Israeli Basketball Super League|2009–10 Israeli Super League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.basket.co.il/BoxScore.asp?GameID=5232&lang=en |title=BOX SCORE: Maccabi T-A Vs Nahariya – Winner League |publisher=Basket.co.il |access-date=September 14, 2013}} In December 2009, he asked to be loaned out again, after the minority of minutes he was receiving. ===Return to Gilboa Galil (2009–2011)=== Mekel was loaned back to Gilboa/Galil, just 6 months after he finished his first loan to the same team.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/62668/180/maccabi-releases-guard-gal-mekel-on-loan |title=Maccabi releases guard Gal Mekel on loan |publisher=Euroleague|date=December 2, 2009 |access-date=September 14, 2013}} In Galil, Mekel shared the point guard position with [[Jeremy Pargo]]. Together, they led Galil to their second Israeli Super League title, after surprising Maccabi in the league's [[2009–10 Israeli Final Four|final]]. Mekel was a key member in the team averaging, 7.5 points and 4.3 assists per game, in 25.5 minutes per game. In 2010, Mekel got offers from the Israeli clubs [[Bnei HaSharon]] and [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]], but he decided to stay in Galil, signing a one-year contract with them.{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/74801/180/galil-holds-on-to-point-guard-mekel |title=Galil holds on to point guard Mekel |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=August 11, 2010 |access-date=September 14, 2013}} He played with the team in the [[Euroleague 2010–11 qualifying rounds|EuroLeague 2010–11 qualifying rounds]], but didn't help the team to pass the qualification's first round, where they were eliminated by [[KK Hemofarm]], from Serbia. At the Israeli national domestic level, Mekel led Galil to a 2nd-place finish at the end of the regular season. They were able to repeat their previous season's trip to the league's final, once again against Maccabi, but this time they lost. Mekel also had a great individual season, which concluded in him winning the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP|Israeli Super League MVP]] award.{{Cite web|url=http://basket.co.il/history.asp?cYear=2011&id=39|title=מנהלת ליגת העל בכדורסל | עונת 2010-11 | היסטוריה|website=basket.co.il}} He was the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Statistical Leaders#Assists leaders|Israeli Premier League Assists Leader]] in 2011. He also played in the [[2011 BSL All-Star Game]]. ===Benetton Treviso (2011–2012)=== On July 5, 2011, Mekel signed a two-year contract with the Italian team [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/29165/benetton-treviso-announces-gal-mekel.html |title=Benetton Treviso announces Gal Mekel |publisher=Sportando.net |access-date=September 14, 2013}} With Benetton, he reached the [[2011–12 Eurocup Basketball#Last 16|2011–12 EuroCup Last 16]], and finished in 11th place in the Italian [[2011–12 Lega Basket Serie A|2011–12 LBA]] league. He averaged 6.3 points and 3.7 assists per game in the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]], and 4 points and 2 assists per game in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. At the end of the season, the club ceased the activity of the first team, focusing on youth sector. ===Maccabi Haifa (2012–2013)=== [[Image:Gal Mekel.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Mekel with Maccabi Haifa in June 2013]] At the start of the 2012–13 season, Mekel wanted to stay with a club that was playing in European-wide competitions, but he also had tryouts with the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[NBA]];{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/truehoop/post/_/id/50101 |title=Jazz impressed by Israel's Mekel |date=October 2012 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=October 28, 2020}} however, after not receiving a sufficient contract offer from the Jazz, he agreed to terms with the Israeli club [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]].{{cite web|author=Art-Up |url=http://www.mhbasket.co.il/News.asp?id=1660&lang=en#.UheM-GT08Vk |title=Gal Mekel joins Maccabi Haifa |publisher=Mhbasket.co.il |access-date=September 14, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131008001726/http://www.mhbasket.co.il/News.asp?id=1660 |archive-date=October 8, 2013 |df=mdy }} Mekel led the team to a 2nd-place finish at the end of the Israeli Super League regular season, and to the [[Israeli Basketball State Cup|Israeli State Cup]] final, where they lost to Maccabi Tel Aviv. Haifa got another chance at a title that season, when they reached the [[2012–13 Israeli Basketball Super League#Final|Israeli Super league's final]], which was held at their home court of [[Romema Arena]]. The Greens went on to win the match and the championship, after a great performance from Mekel: 21 points and 7 assists,{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Israel/2013/0613_159_2732.asp |title=Finals Game 1: Maccabi T-A – Maccabi Haifa 79–86 |publisher=Eurobasket.com |date=June 13, 2013 |access-date=September 14, 2013}} after which he received the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League MVP|Israeli League MVP]] award, which he had won a night before.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sport5.co.il/articles.aspx?FolderID=274&docID=144389|title=ב-2011 זה לא הספיק לו: גל מקל זכה בתואר שחקן העונה - ספורט 5|website=Sport5.co.il - אתר ערוץ הספורט|date=June 13, 2013 }} ===Dallas Mavericks (2013–2014)=== On July 11, 2013, the [[Dallas Mavericks]] signed Mekel to a three-year minimum fully guaranteed contract, and he became the second Israeli to join the NBA.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/11/mavs-sign-mekel.ap/ |title=Mavs sign Israeli League MVP guard Mekel |work=NBA.com |date=July 11, 2013 |access-date=September 14, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217164444/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/11/mavs-sign-mekel.ap/ |archive-date=February 17, 2015 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4697398 |title=Dollars and Sense: Gal Mekel |work=ESPN.com |date=September 6, 2013 |access-date=October 28, 2020}} Mekel played with the Mavericks in the [[2013 NBA Summer League]], and finished with averages of 9.7 points and 5 assists per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2013/players/sl_gal_mekel/ |title=2013 Summer League Statistics |work=NBA.com |access-date=September 14, 2013}} In his debut regular season game for the Mavs on October 30, 2013, Mekel recorded 2 points, 2 rebounds, and 3 assists in a 118–109 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20131030/ATLDAL/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Mavericks 118, Hawks 109 |work=Nba.com |access-date=November 9, 2013}} Two Israeli players played on opposing NBA teams for the first time on November 1 when Mekel and the Mavericks played [[Omri Casspi]] and the Rockets. The two had been teammates on the Israeli Under-16, Under-18, and Under-20 teams, and on the Maccabi Tel Aviv junior team.{{cite web|last=Zeevi |first=Elad |url=https://www.haaretz.com/news/sports/1.555779 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105175518/http://www.haaretz.com/news/sports/1.555779 |archive-date=November 5, 2013 |title=Casspi and Mekel both shine in first-ever Israeli NBA face-off |publisher=Haaretz |date=November 2, 2013 |access-date=September 30, 2015}}{{cite web |url=http://blog.chron.com/ultimaterockets/2013/11/historic-meeting-for-gal-mekel-and-omri-casspi/ |title=Ultimate Rockets » Historic meeting for Gal Mekel and Omri Casspi |publisher=chron.com |date=November 1, 2013 |access-date=November 9, 2013 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052901/http://blog.chron.com/ultimaterockets/2013/11/historic-meeting-for-gal-mekel-and-omri-casspi/ |url-status=dead }} In that game, the Houston Rockets beat the Dallas Mavericks 113–105 in Houston. Casspi scored 12 points in 21 minutes, and Mekel scored 11 points and dished off 6 assists in 23 minutes in his best NBA game to date. On November 30, he started in his first NBA game against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and scored 6 points and dished off 7 assists in 26 minutes. The Mavs lost that game though, 106–112. After the game on January 13, 2014, Mekel was placed on the injured list due to a torn [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] in his right knee, which required surgery and at least 4–6 weeks of recovery.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/mavericks/2014/01/17/gal-mekel-knee-injury-meniscus-dallas-israel/4588639/|title=Dallas Mavericks' Gal Mekel out after knee surgery|website=USA TODAY}} On March 4, 2014, Mekel was assigned to the [[Texas Legends]] of the NBA D-League.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-assign-gal-mekel-to-texas-legends/|title=Mavericks Assign Gal Mekel to Texas Legends|date=March 4, 2014}} On March 9, he was recalled by the Mavericks.{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15434|title=Mavs recall Gal Mekel from D-League – NBA Blog|date=March 9, 2014 }} On March 15, he was reassigned to the Legends.{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15488|title=Mavs recall Shane Larkin, re-assign Gal Mekel to D-League – NBA Blog|date=March 15, 2014 }} He was recalled three days later. On October 29, 2014, Mekel was waived by the Mavericks.{{Cite web|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2014/10/29/mavericks-sign-j-j-barea-waive-gal-mekel/|title=Mavericks sign J.J. Barea, waive Gal Mekel|first=Dan|last=Feldman|date=October 30, 2014}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2014)=== On December 5, 2014, Mekel signed a two-year, non-guaranteed contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-gal-mekel|title=Pelicans Sign Gal Mekel|website=New Orleans Pelicans}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/pelicans/article_d35efe2e-4413-5720-b119-cde14b1bc146.html|title=Newly signed Pelicans' Gal Mekel aiming to impact games with his passing|first=John|last=Reid|website=NOLA.com|date=December 8, 2014 }} However, he was later waived by the Pelicans on December 19 after appearing in just four games.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-gal-mekel|title=Pelicans Waive Gal Mekel|website=New Orleans Pelicans}} ===Nizhny Novgorod (2015)=== On February 24, 2015, Mekel moved to Russia, and signed with [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]], until the end of the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Nizhny Novgorod adds guard Mekel|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5rxrvhmshuvvch64|access-date=February 24, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=February 24, 2015}} Nizhny Novgorod's [[2014–15 VTB United League]] season was ended, after being eliminated by [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] 3–0 in their [[VTB United League]] semifinal playoff series. In July 2015, he parted ways with Nizhny.{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/168390/gal-mekel-pays-dollars50000-and-leaves-nizhny-novogorod.html|title=Gal Mekel pays $50.000 and leaves Nizhny Novogorod}} ===Crvena zvezda (2015)=== On August 27, 2015, Mekel signed a one-year contract with Serbian [[ABA League]] team [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]].{{cite news|title=Crvena Zvezda tabs Mekel for backcourt|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/6aregx8nhte9d9pe|access-date=27 August 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=27 August 2015}} However, on December 3, 2015, Mekel parted ways with Crvena zvezda after appearing in 13 games. ===Third stint with Maccabi (2016–2017)=== On January 10, 2016, Mekel returned to [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] for a third stint, signing a 3½-year contract.{{cite news|title=Mekel returns to Maccabi Tel Aviv, Farmar out|url=https://www.jpost.com/Israel-News/Sports/Mekel-returns-to-Maccabi-Tel-Aviv-Farmar-out-441065|access-date=January 10, 2016|work=jpost.com|date=January 10, 2016}} Mekel won the [[Israeli Basketball State Cup|Israeli State Cup]] titles in 2016 and 2017, earning the Finals MVP honors for two consecutive years.{{cite news|url=https://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=13140 |script-title=he:"אמרתי לפניני שלא נצא מפה בלי הגביע" |work=basket.co.il |date=February 17, 2017 |access-date=October 6, 2018|language=he}} He was the Israeli Premier League Assists Leader in 2016. On July 4, 2017, Mekel parted ways with Maccabi.{{cite news|author=E. Carchia |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/239828/gal-mekel-maccabi-tel-aviv-part-ways.html |title=Gal Mekel, Maccabi Tel Aviv part ways |work=Sportando |date=July 4, 2017 |access-date=July 1, 2017}} ===Gran Canaria (2017–2018)=== On July 14, 2017, Mekel signed a one-year deal with the Spanish team [[CB Gran Canaria|Herbalife Gran Canaria]].{{cite news|title=Gal Mekel será uno de los bases del Herbalife Gran Canaria|url=https://cbgrancanaria.net/noticias/liga-endesa/gal-mekel-sera-uno-los-bases-del-herbalife-gran-canaria/|access-date=14 July 2017|work=Club Baloncesto Gran Canaria|date=14 July 2017|language=es-ES}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} In 17 EuroCup games, he averaged 9.6 points and 5 assists per game. Mekel helped Gran Canaria to reach the [[2017–18 EuroCup Basketball Playoffs|2018 EuroCup Quarterfinals]], as well as reaching the [[2018 ACB Playoffs|2018 ACB Semifinals]], which helped them earn a qualification to the [[2018–19 EuroLeague|EuroLeague]] as the highest-placed team in the Liga ACB without a long-term EuroLeague licence. ===Zenit Saint Petersburg (2018–2019)=== On October 8, 2018, Mekel signed with the Russian team [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] for the 2018–19 season.{{cite news|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/96fwwktopjtqhci7/zenit-brings-in-experienced-guard-mekel |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181009132520/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/96fwwktopjtqhci7/zenit-brings-in-experienced-guard-mekel |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 9, 2018 |title=Zenit brings in experienced guard Mekel |work=EuroCupBasketball.com |date=October 8, 2018 |access-date=October 8, 2018}} In 27 games played in the [[VTB United League|VTB League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]], he averaged 7.4 points, 5.3 assists and 1.9 rebounds in 18.8 minutes per game. Mekel helped Zenit reach the [[2018–19 VTB United League|2019 VTB League Semifinals]], where they eventually were eliminated by [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]]. On July 7, 2019, Mekel parted ways with Zenit.{{cite news | title=Gal Mekel leaves Zenit St. Petersburg | url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gal-mekel-leaves-zenit-st-petersburg/ | work=Sportando.basketball | date=July 7, 2019 |access-date=July 7, 2019}} ===Grissin Bon Reggio Emilia (2019–2020)=== On August 15, 2019, Mekel signed with [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Grissin Bon Reggio Emilia]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite news|title=Gal Mekel signs with Reggio Emilia|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gal-mekel-signs-with-reggio-emilia/|date=August 15, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|access-date=August 15, 2019|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} On October 20, 2019, Mekel recorded a season-high 21 points in 27 minutes, shooting 7-of-13 from the field, along with five assists, leading Reggio Emilia to an 84–72 win over [[OriOra Pistoia]].{{Cite web|title=Grissin Bon Reggio Emilia - OriOra Pistoia 84-72|url=https://web.legabasket.it/game/1672545/grissin_bon_reggio_emilia-oriora_pistoia-84:72|date=October 20, 2019|publisher=LegaBasket.it|access-date=October 21, 2019}} Mekel parted ways with the club due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy|coronavirus infection]] in [[Italy]]. ===Unicaja Malaga (2020–2021)=== On March 5, 2020, he signed with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/unicaja-malaga-signs-gal-mekel/|title=Unicaja Malaga signs Gal Mekel|date=March 5, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=March 5, 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} ===MoraBanc Andorra (2021–2022)=== On October 11, 2021, he has signed with [[BC Andorra|MoraBanc Andorra]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/gal-mekel-signs-with-morabanc-andorra/|title=Gal Mekel signs with MoraBanc Andorra|last=|first=|date=October 11, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=October 11, 2021|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} ==National team career== Mekel is a member of the [[Israel national basketball team]]. He participated in the [[EuroBasket 2009|2009]], [[EuroBasket 2011|2011]], [[EuroBasket 2015|2015]] and [[EuroBasket 2017|2017]] [[EuroBasket]] tournaments. ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player
